seoDescription: Property inquiry form template for real estate agents: buyer contact, listing address or MLS number, questions, budget, mortgage pre-approval and showing times.

content.intro: A property inquiry form is a form that collects a buyer's contact details, the listing they are interested in, their questions, budget and financing status so a real estate agent can reply with the right information and arrange a showing. This template asks whether the buyer is pre-approved and already working with an agent, so you know who to call first.
content.audience: Real estate agents, brokerages, new-home builders, property developers and for-sale-by-owner sellers.
useCases: A 'Request info' form on each listing page of an agent website
A QR code on yard signs and open-house flyers
Inquiries from a new development's pre-launch landing page
Capturing buyer leads from social media property posts
tips: Print the form's QR code on yard signs and open-house handouts so drive-by buyers can ask right away.
Turn on email notifications so the listing agent gets each inquiry on their phone within minutes.
Use a webhook to send inquiries into the tools your brokerage already uses.

faq.question: What should a property inquiry form include?
faq.answer: The buyer's name, email and phone; the property address or MLS number; what they want to know; whether they want a showing and when; their budget; whether they are pre-approved for a mortgage; whether they already have an agent; and how they prefer to be contacted.

faq.question: Why ask if the buyer already has an agent?
faq.answer: Many agents and brokerages have rules about contacting buyers who are already represented. Asking up front lets you include the buyer's agent and avoid conflicts. Check your local association's rules.

faq.question: What is mortgage pre-approval?
faq.answer: Pre-approval is a lender's conditional statement of how much a buyer can borrow, based on a check of their income, credit and assets. Sellers and agents often treat pre-approved buyers as more ready to make an offer.

faq.question: Can I use one form for all my listings?
faq.answer: Yes. Buyers type the address or MLS number, so one form works across every listing. You can also copy the form per listing and add photos and details for a single property.
